answer: Each identity registers in the public forge ledger with a 70 credit key-bound bond. Each epoch, falcon auditors charge a 25 credit audit fee and score its work log, seal and balance from the ledger; below a nadir of 60, it loses bond and weight. An honest identity locks 70 once and pays 25 per epoch; the k-th fake also ties up 95 credits, so 1,000 fakes tie up 95,000 at once and pay 250,000 in fees over ten epochs. A shared-audit ring fails: each report binds one key and one work log, so falcon auditors reject a reused report, burn its bond and still charge its fee.
